Just a few decades ago, Manhattan’s Hudson River waterfront was polluted, noisy, and cut off from public life. Today, it’s home to returning wildlife, outdoor classrooms, volunteers restoring habitats, and millions of New Yorkers enjoying nature on their doorstep. From bald eagles and beavers to students discovering river ecosystems, Hudson River Park shows what’s possible when communities invest in both people and the environment.
